comments.body: Correction and critique, 2026-10-24. The description is wrong that msg post --to @human with no --group lands in a group of just that agent and the human: it goes to the one group they already share, which may hold others, is refused if they share several, and makes a pair group only if they share none (docs/cli/msg.md, Groups). The quick ask still works, without that guarantee. From the Codex critique, checked against the code: (1) Freeze the group, sequence number and author shown in the banner into its payload; today it carries only daemon and group (Notifications.swift:210), and each new message replaces the group's banner, so a reply resolved at callback time could go to whoever posted last. (2) A banner reply must not read the group: MsgRequest.Read takes only a group and moves the human's cursor to the head, so answering otter's banner would also clear heron's unseen question. Simplest first version: a banner reply leaves the read cursor alone. (3) @muster's banners are not replyable: @muster is never a valid addressee. (4) Keep the reply on failure and offer a way to recover it; never retry a post whose outcome is unknown.

description: A message for the human today raises a macOS notification that says only how many wait and from whom ("2 messages for you from heron, otter", MessageNotification.body), so answering even a yes-or-no question means opening the transcript tab. Agreed in the Lectern page muster-group-conversation (2026-10-24) as the part of the group conversation work to ship first: Muster draws a banner of its own in the window, in Swift and SwiftUI, showing the newest message's text with a reply field, and offered answers as buttons once a_2naAat73L lands. The reply posts to that message's author, in that group, as @human. The owner, 2026-10-24: no macOS notification is how the human interacts with messages; "the more vertically integrated we are, the better an experience we can deliver with Muster, as we learned when we got rid of herdr." That gives agents a quick way to ask something small with no new verb: msg post --to @human. Without --group it goes to the one group the agent and the human share, or a new two-member group if they share none, and is refused if they share several. What the daemon tells windows about messages waiting for the human carries counts and authors, not text, so it has to send the newest message's text as well. The comments hold the critique's rules for this banner: freeze the message it shows, leave the read cursor alone on reply, never offer a reply to @muster, keep the text on failure.
title: Muster's own banner shows a message and takes a reply
